newsitem.title: GERMANY: German coffee buyers make provisions for Christmas.
newsitem.headline: German coffee buyers make provisions for Christmas.

text.p: German physical coffee markets were gearing up for higher volume business during a seasonal peak in roasted coffee demand at Christmas, traders said on Monday.
"Nearby supplies of quality Central Americans and Colombians are tight and prices will remain high for another three to four months," one said.
"Roasters have bought competitively priced Brazils to meet volume requirements for the Christmas season but this alone won't be sufficient to maintain roasting qualities."
"Futures will reflect this through a high nearby premium."
Consumption in 1996 would only be steady and stocks in Bremen and Hamburg were described as more comfortable than elsewhere in global consumption centres.
But a severe winter could boost roasted coffee consumption and roasters had reflected this possibility in active recent purchases, traders said.
"There was good business at the end of October and early November when futures were some 10-15 cents lower," another trader said.

New York Dec arabicas ended a choppy week lower at 125.85 cents/lb on Friday, with speculative profit-taking accompanied by scale-down roaster buying. Traders said the market now looked technically vulnerable on the downside.
Brazilian differentials eased in local import markets while Colombian and Central American exporters raised theirs and sellers of African arabicas also found interest at higher prices.
Outright prices of robustas increased in sympathy with arabicas but supply was plentiful from all origins and this discouraged transactions.

Dec shipment Brazils were on offer at $111 per 50 kg fob versus $110 a week earlier. Colombians, at $150, were up $10 while Kenyans were at $169, up $9. Indonesian robustas rose $7 on the week to $68. --Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
